blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In text-to-video retrieval, MLLM-based embedding models do well when the text describes the scene (general retrieval), but poorly when it describes actions and their direction (time-sensitive retrieval). TARA, a pioneering work, fine-tunes such a model on text triplets with temporal hard negatives; it improves time-sensitive retrieval but lowers general retrieval (mean R@1 over six benchmarks in our rerun on Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B: 58.4->44.8), and its released model keeps general retrieval only when ensembled with Qwen3-VL-Embedding. Our goal is strong general and time-sensitive retrieval with one model and one vector per clip. Three findings lead to three simple components. Keep loss: general retrieval follows how far the output embeddings drift from the base model, not how far the weights move; we therefore keep them near the base model, which keeps most general retrieval even without general-domain data. Pair loss: the text embeddings of an action description and its reversed-direction version are well separated, but the video embeddings of a clip and its reversed copy are close; we therefore widen the gap between the video embeddings of each clip and its reversed copy, in the direction of the difference between their two text embeddings. Middle-layer LoRA: frames are combined in the middle layers, and temporal information peaks in or just after them; we therefore train LoRA only on these layers, which nearly matches training all weights on most time-sensitive benchmarks with 0.15% of the parameters and keeps general retrieval better. General R@1 stays at 58.4, while R@1 with each clip's reversed copy in the gallery rises from 55.5 to 63.2; the gains carry over to unseen benchmarks and InternVL2-8B-RA. The keep loss is also a remedy for the TARA recipe (general R@1: 44.8->57.8), and ensembling TARA with Ours gives the highest scores on RTime and unseen CiA among the compared models.
blocks.zh: 在文本到视频检索中,基于MLLM的嵌入模型在文本描述场景(一般检索)时表现良好,但在描述动作及其方向(时间敏感检索)时表现不佳. TARA是一个开创性的作品,它用时间硬底片对文本三进制的这种模型进行微调;它改进了时间敏锐的检索,但降低了一般检索(在Qune3-VL-Embedding-8B: 58.4->44.8上我们重播时,平均R@1高于6个基准),其所发布的模型只在与Qune3-VL-Embedding共演时才保持了一般检索. 我们的目标是用一个模型和每个片段一个矢量来进行强有力的一般和对时间敏感的检索。 三个结论导致三个简单的部分。 保持亏损:一般检索跟随输出嵌入从基模型漂移到多远,而不是重量移动多远;因此,我们保持它们靠近基模型,即使没有一般域数据,也保持了大多数一般检索. 平面丢失:一个动作描述所嵌入的文字及其倒向方向的版本是完全分开的,但是一个剪辑所嵌入的视频及其倒向拷贝是相近的;因此,我们扩大每个剪辑所嵌入的视频与其倒向拷贝之间的间隙,取其两个文本嵌入的区别方向. 中层 LORA: 框架在中层结合,时间信息在中间或紧接在中间;因此,我们只在这些层上培训LORA, 几乎将大多数时间敏感基准上的所有权重都与0.15%的参数相匹配,并更好地保持一般检索。 R@1将军停留在58.4,而R@1在画廊里反向复制的每个片段,则从55.5个增加到63.2个;收益转入隐形基准和InternVL2-8B-RA。 保留损失也是TARA配方(一般R@1:44.8->57.8)的补救方法,同我们的共鸣TARA在比较模型中给出了RTime和CiA的最高分.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Embedding models built on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) retrieve videos well but are weak when the text query is about what happens over time: when the direction of a motion decides the action.
On Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B [ 29 ] (Qwen), Recall@1 (R@1) is 56.1 56.1 on MSR-VTT [ 50 ] , whose queries mostly describe what is visible, but only 22.4 22.4 on SSv2-Template [ 28 ] , whose queries describe actions.
On RTime [ 7 ] , R@1 falls from 89.5 89.5 to 55.5 55.5 when the reversed copy of each clip (see Fig. 1 a for an example) is added to the gallery. We call this RTime Hard.
blocks.zh:
嵌入模型建立在多模式大语言模型(MLLM)上,可以很好地取回视频,但当文本查询是有关随时间而发生的事情:当运动的方向决定动作时会很弱.
在Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B [29] (Quen)上,Recall@1 (R@1)在MSR-VTT [50]上是56.1 56.1,他们的询问大多描述了可见的东西,而SSv2-Template [28]上只有22.4 22.4,他们的询问描述了行动.
在"RTime [7]"上,R@1从89.5 89.5跌至55.5 55.5,每段片段的倒转拷贝(以图1 a为例)被加到画廊上. 我们称这为"难时"

blocks.en:
Training for time-sensitive retrieval improves it but lowers general retrieval performance.
With the recipe of TARA [ 3 ] , which fine-tunes on text triplets with temporal hard negatives, the mean general R@1 of Qwen falls from 58.4 58.4 to 44.8 44.8 ( Sec. 5 ). The released TARA model keeps general retrieval only when ensembled with Qwen, which needs a second embedding model and a vector twice as long.
Plain training (Plain: contrastive losses on time-sensitive data, with no constraint on the embeddings) also lowers general R@1, to 54.7 54.7 with low-rank adapters (LoRA) [ 16 ] and to 50.1 50.1 with all weights of the language model ( Fig. 1 b).
blocks.zh:
时间敏感的检索培训可以改进,但降低一般检索性能。
由于TARA[3]的配方对文本三重体进行微调并带有时间硬底片,Quen中的平均一般R@1从58.4 58.4下降到44.8 44.8 (sec. 5.). 所发行的TARA模型只保留了与Qwen共聚时的一般取回,需要第二个嵌入模型和两倍长的向量.
平面训练(Plain:在时间敏感数据上出现对比性损失,对嵌入没有约束)还将一般R@1降低到54.7 54.7分并配有低等适配器(Lora) [16];将语言模型所有分量(图1b)降低到50.1分.

blocks.en:
We ask whether a model with one vector per clip can improve on time-sensitive queries while preserving general R@1 performance.
Three observations ( Sec. 3 ) suggest three hypotheses.
First, Plain training moves the clip embeddings away from those of the base model and breaks their neighborhoods. (H1) Holding the output embeddings near those of the base model keeps general retrieval.
Second, the text embeddings of an action description and its reversed-direction version are well separated, but the video embeddings of a clip and its reversed copy are close. (H2) Pushing each clip away from its reversed copy raises time-sensitive retrieval.
Third, layer-wise probes and attention blocking show that frames are combined in the middle layers. Temporal information peaks in or just after them (L15–L28 on Qwen) and then fades. (H3) Training these layers gains more than training only the later layers.
blocks.zh:
我们询问,每个片段有一个向量的模型在保留一般的R@1性能的同时,是否能够改进对时间敏感的查询。
三种观察(第3条)提出三种假设。
首先,Plain train 将嵌入的夹子从基底模型的夹子中移出,并打破了他们的街区. (H1) 持有靠近基模型的输出嵌入物保持了一般检索.
第二,一个动作描述及其倒向方向版本的嵌入文本被很好地分隔开来,但一个剪辑的视频嵌入及其倒向副本是相近的. (H2) 将每个剪辑从倒转的拷贝中推开,可增加时间敏感的检索。
第三,分层探测器和注意力阻隔显示,帧被组合在中层. 时间信息在它们内部或紧接其后(Quen上的L15-L28)会达到顶峰并逐渐消退. (H3) 培训这些层次比仅培训后面的层次获得更多的收益。

blocks.en:
Our recipe (Ours) follows the hypotheses. Starting from Plain training, we add a keep loss on the output embeddings (H1) and a pair-margin loss on each clip and its own reversed copy (H2), which pushes the difference of their video embeddings toward the difference of their text embeddings. We train LoRA on the middle layers (H3).
Each part is known: the keep loss is an output anchor, as in LwF [ 32 ] and BCT [ 41 ] , and reversed clips serve as negatives in earlier work [ 4 , 7 ] . Our contribution is the analysis that says which parts are needed and why. Interpolating the weights of Ours without the keep loss toward the base model (WiSE-FT [ 48 ] ) reaches about the same point as Ours, as H1 predicts. The keep loss achieves this in a single run, without choosing the interpolation weight.
blocks.zh:
我们的食谱,遵循了各种猜想。 从Plain训练开始,我们增加输出嵌入(H1)的保存损失,以及每个片段的双边损失和它自己的倒置副本(H2),这把它们嵌入的视频的差异推向了它们文本嵌入的不同. 我们训练LORA在中层(H3).
每个部分都是已知的:保存损失是一个输出锚,如LwF [32]和BCT [41]中,倒置的片段在更早的作品[4,7]中充当了底片. 我们的贡献是分析需要哪些部分以及为什么。 如H1所预测, 将我们的权重内入, 而不向基模型(WISE-FT [48])损失。 保存损失在一次运行中实现这一点,而不选择插值重量.

blocks.en: With one vector per clip, Ours keeps general R@1 at 58.4 58.4 , while RTime Hard rises from 55.5 55.5 to 63.2 63.2 and retrieval of opposite actions on two unseen benchmarks from Chirality in Action (CiA) [ 2 ] , CiA-Charades and CiA-EPIC, gains 11 11 and 13 13 points, mostly through frame order. The results hold on InternVL2-8B-RA.

blocks.en: Our contributions are: • Output drift (H1). Across 28 28 variants, general R@1 tracks how close the output embeddings stay to those of the base model, not how far the weights move. This holds whether a loss keeps them close during training or weight interpolation restores them after training. Keeping the weights near their initial values during training (L2-SP, a lower learning rate) preserves less general R@1. With a keep loss, Ours keeps most general retrieval even without general-domain data and lies above WiSE-FT of Plain training, and the loss restores general R@1 in the TARA recipe ( Secs. 3 , 5 and 6 ). • Direction gap (H2). The video embeddings of a clip and its reversed copy are close, while the text embeddings of their descriptions are well separated. A pair-margin loss that widens the gap between these two video embeddings toward the difference of their text embeddings raises time-sensitive retrieval on two models, including opposite actions on unseen benchmarks ( Secs. 3 , 4 and 5 ). • Middle-layer peak (H3). Temporal information peaks in or just after the middle layers, where frames are combined, and then fades, unlike appearance. LoRA on these layers, with 0.15 % 0.15\% of the parameters, raises RTime and unseen CiA nearly as much as all weights and keeps general R@1 better ( Secs. 3 and 5 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献是:产出漂移(H1)。 横跨28个变体,一般R@1跟踪输出嵌入方式如何与基准模型的嵌入方式相接,而不是加权移动多远. 也就是说,损失是否在培训期间使他们保持接近,或者在培训后进行体重插入恢复。 将权重保持在培训期间的初始值附近(L2-SP,学习率较低),保留了较低的一般R@1. 有了保留损失,我们的系统即使没有普通域数据,也保留了大多数一般检索,并且位于Plain训练的WISE-FT之上,损失还原了TARA食谱中的普通R@1(secs. 3, 5和6.). • 方向差距(H2)。 一个片段的视频嵌入及其倒置的拷贝是相近的,而其描述的文本嵌入则被很好的隔开. 双边损耗扩大了这两段视频在文本嵌入差异上的差距,使两个模型的检索具有时间敏感性,包括在无形基准上的相反行动(第3、4和5节)。 • 中层高峰(H3)。 时间信息在中间地层或紧接中间地层后会达到峰值,框被组合而后会逐渐淡出,与外观不同. 这些层上的LORA, 0. 15% 0. 15% 的参数, 提高 RTime 和看不见的 CiA 几乎等于所有重量, 并保持一般的 R@1 更好(secs. 3 and 5) 。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Many works turn MLLMs into one-vector embedders, trained on text [ 18 , 46 ] , text and images [ 19 , 35 ] , captioning then text [ 51 ] or large multimodal sets [ 36 , 26 , 11 , 12 , 29 ] . MARS [ 20 ] keeps several vectors.
These models target general retrieval. We adapt such a model to time-sensitive retrieval.
blocks.zh:
许多作品将 MLLMs 变成单调嵌入器, 训练有素的文本 [18, 46], 文本和图像 [19, 35], 标题然后是文本 [51] 或大型多式集 [36, 26, 11, 12, 29]. MARS [20] 保留了几种向量.
这些模型针对一般检索. 我们改用这种模式来进行时间敏感的检索。

blocks.en:
Single frames solve many video-language tasks [ 28 ] , so new benchmarks test the order of events and the direction of motion [ 28 , 7 , 2 , 30 , 22 ] .
Training methods add temporal hard negatives such as reordered or reversed clips [ 4 , 47 , 7 , 44 ] or temporal antonym captions in TARA [ 3 ] , which is trained on text data alone.
We also use reversed clips and find that a loss pairing each clip with its own reversed copy gains more than stronger hard negatives.
On a strong embedder, the released TARA model keeps general R@1 only when ensembled with Qwen3-VL-Embedding, and ViTAL-X [ 44 ] starts from a frozen SigLIP 2. We fine-tune a strong embedder and keep its general R@1 with one model and one vector per clip.
blocks.zh:
单帧可以解决许多视频语言任务[28],因此新的基准测试事件的顺序和运动方向[28,7,2,30,22].
培训方法增加了时间硬底片,如重排或倒转的片段[4,47,7,44] 或TARA[3]中的时间定名标题,仅培训文本数据。
我们还使用倒置的片段,发现每段片段的损失与自己倒置的复制收益配对,比更强烈的硬底片要多.
在一个坚固的嵌入器上,所释放的TARA模型只保留了一般的R@1,当同Qwen3-VL-Embedding合唱时,而VITAL-X[44]从被冻结的SigLIP开始. 2. 联合国 我们微调一个坚固的嵌入器,并保持其一般的R@1,每片中有一个模型和一个矢量.

blocks.en:
Studies of video LLMs for question answering find that temporal reasoning starts in the early to middle layers [ 24 , 42 ] and that temporal information fades near the output [ 45 , 43 ] . Several methods recover it [ 43 , 33 , 8 , 14 , 52 ] . Blocking attention between frames in all layers, however, costs little question-answering accuracy [ 10 ] .
In retrieval, a middle layer of a video MLLM can retrieve better than the final layer without training [ 46 ] , and MLLM and CLIP retrievers gain from fusing features of several layers [ 20 , 34 ] . These works fuse or select layers but do not ask what those layers encode. We measure temporal information layer by layer and then train the middle layers, keeping one vector from the final layer.
blocks.zh:
对用于回答问题的视频LLMs的研究发现,时间推理开始于早期到中层[24,42],时间信息逐渐淡出接近输出[45,43]. 有几种方法可以回收[43、33、8、14、52]。 然而,将注意力堵住各个层次的帧之间,代价很小的回答准确性[10].
在取回过程中,一段视频MLLM的中层可以比最后一层更好的取回,而不经过训练[46],而MLLM和CLIP取回器则从多层的引信特性得到[20,34]. 这些工作引信或选择地层,但不问这些地层编码是什么。 我们逐层测量时间信息层,然后训练中层,从最后层中保持一个向量.

blocks.en: Embedding differences that are parallel to text differences appear in word embeddings [ 37 ] , and directional losses enforce them in CLIP-guided generation and editing [ 9 , 23 , 5 ] and in PC-CLIP [ 40 ] . Our pair loss ( Sec. 4 ) is related: it pushes the difference between the video embeddings of a clip and its reversed copy toward the difference between the text embeddings of their two descriptions. Before It Fades [ 43 ] also uses a forward-minus-reversed difference, but without training: it injects the difference of hidden states into later layers at inference time. We find that widening the video difference matters more than aligning the two differences, and that the text difference must come from the same pair.
blocks.zh: 嵌入与文本差异相平行的差异出现在词嵌入[37]中,方向损失在CLIP导出和编辑[9,23,5]和PC-CLIP[40]中强制执行. 我们的对子损失(sec. 4)是相关的:它把一个片段的视频嵌入与它反向复制之间的区别推向两个片段的文本嵌入之间的区别. 在它Fades [43] 之前,也使用前倒倒倒相差法,但没有经过训练:在推论时间将隐藏状态的差法注入后上层. 我们发现,扩大视频差异比调整两个差异更重要,文本差异必须来自同对.

blocks.en:
Continual learning, distillation and backward-compatible training preserve old abilities or embeddings with output, relation or weight constraints [ 32 , 25 , 15 , 39 , 41 , 49 , 6 ] , and frozen teachers protect generalization when adapting CLIP [ 21 , 17 ] .
When fine-tuning CLIP for image classification, keeping the features near the pretrained ones reduces forgetting, by matching the features of several layers (LDIFS [ 38 ] ), distilling on reference data [ 54 ] or training the head first [ 27 ] . LDIFS finds the last-layer features alone not enough there. Video embedders change the base only a little, through LoRA [ 16 , 13 , 44 ] or a small training set [ 3 ] , but add no output anchor. For MLLM video embedders, we find that holding the output embeddings near the base model, not the weights, keeps general retrieval, even with a loss alone and no reference data. Weight interpolation (WiSE-FT [ 48 ] ) keeps general R@1 through the same closeness ( Sec. 6 ).
blocks.zh:
不断学习,分馏和后向相容培训保留了老能力或有输出,关系或重量限制的嵌入[32,25,15,39,41,49,6],被冻结的教师在适应CLIP[21,17]时保护通俗化.
在为图像分类而微调CLIP时,通过匹配多层的特征(LDIFS [38]),在参考数据上分馏[54]或先训练头部[27]来将特征保持在被预先训练的特征附近会减少遗忘. LDIFS发现仅靠最后一层特性是不够的. 视频嵌入器只稍有改变地基,通过LORA[16,13,44]或一个小型的训练集[3],但没有添加输出锚. 对于 MLLM 视频嵌入器,我们发现,在底模附近持有输出嵌入,而不是权重,保持了一般的检索,即使只有丢失,也没有参考数据. 重量内插(WISE-FT [48])通过相同的相近度(Sec.

blocks.en: 3 What Plain Training Changes
blocks.zh: 3个 培训的改变

blocks.en: We study Plain training and then the base models, Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B (Qwen) and InternVL2-8B-RA (InternVL). Each observation suggests a hypothesis (H1–H3) that becomes one part of our method ( Sec. 4 ).

blocks.en:
General retrieval performance is measured on six benchmarks whose text queries mostly describe what is visible (MSR-VTT, DiDeMo, ActivityNet, VATEX, MSVD, LSMDC). General R@1 is their mean. Time-sensitive retrieval performance is measured on RTime, CiA and SSv2-T, whose text queries depend on how actions progress over time.
RTime has 990 990 forward test clips and their reversed copies, each with a forward and a reversed text query. The gallery holds the forward clips (RTime Origin) or both (RTime Hard), scored by R@1. In RTime Binary, each query chooses between a clip and its reversed copy (accuracy, chance 50 50 ).
CiA has pairs of opposite actions on SSv2, Charades and EPIC. Each class name is a query, every clip of its class is a positive, and we report mAP. Our main gallery, Chiral, holds the query class and its opposite. Static adds one non-opposite class from every other pair, and All holds every class. CiA-Charades alone means CiA-Charades Chiral.
SSv2-Template (SSv2-T) queries are the 174 174 template names (objects hidden). The template names are also training queries (with other clips), so a gain on SSv2-T does not show transfer to unseen text. SSv2-Label uses the same clips with object-specific queries.
We train on SSv2, RTime and MSR-VTT. CiA-Charades, CiA-EPIC and the five other general benchmarks are unseen . Qwen has 36 36 layers and InternVL 32 32 . Lk: the output of layer k k , counted from 0 0 .

blocks.en:
We train with the base losses of Sec. 4 , which use reversed and shuffled clips as hard negatives, with no term that ties the model to the base model. We call this Plain training. For each MSR-VTT test clip, we take its 10 10 nearest clips by cosine similarity of the output embeddings, before and after training, and call the share that remains the neighbor overlap.
Training all weights of the language model gives a neighbor overlap of only 0.62 0.62 and lowers general R@1 from 58.4 58.4 to 50.1 50.1 ( Fig. 2 a). Low-rank adapters (LoRA) on the middle layers (L12–L23) give 0.65 0.65 and 54.7 54.7 .
The clip embeddings also move away from those of the base model (mean cosine 0.81 0.81 with LoRA). This suggests adding a loss that holds the output embeddings near those of the base model (H1).

On RTime test pairs, the embeddings of a forward and a reversed query are far apart, while those of a forward and a reversed clip are close ( Fig. 2 b).
We call the forward minus the reversed query embedding the language direction d t d_{t} , and the forward minus the reversed clip embedding the video direction d v d_{v} .
Over the 990 990 test pairs, the mean norm is 0.669 0.669 for the language directions but only 0.290 0.290 for the video directions, and the two are nearly orthogonal (mean cosine 0.089 0.089 ). This suggests pushing each clip embedding away from that of its reversed copy (H2).

blocks.en:
We measure the performance of the base models layer by layer in three ways ( Fig. 3 ).
First ( Fig. 3 a, b), we train a small retrieval head on each layer of the frozen model: MSR-VTT keeps rising to the output, while SSv2-T and RTime Hard peak near L28 and then fall. InternVL shows a similar but flatter pattern, with SSv2-T peaking earlier (L15).
Second, linear probes without text ( Fig. 3 c) check that the peak lies in the video embedding itself. The appearance control stays at 79 79 from L25 to the output, while opposite actions peak at L25, and forward versus reversed RTime clips at L15.
Third, we block cross-frame attention at test time: blocking from Lk means that, from layer k k on, tokens of one frame cannot attend to those of other frames. On Qwen, blocking from L12 lowers CiA-SSv2 Chiral by 10.6 10.6 and CiA-SSv2 Static by 8.7 8.7 , while blocking from L24 changes each score by at most 0.5 0.5 . InternVL behaves alike with L8 and L20 ( Appendix F ).
So frames are combined before L24, for appearance and time, and temporal information peaks in or just after the middle layers (L15–L28 on Qwen) and fades toward the output, while appearance does not. This suggests adapting the layers that combine frames, not only the later layers (H3).
blocks.zh:
我们以三种方式(图3)逐层衡量基准模型的性能。
首先(图3a,b),我们在被冻结的模型的每一层上训练一个小取回头: MSR-VTT不断向输出上升,而SSv2-T和RTime Hard则在L28附近达到高峰并随后倒下. InternVL呈现出类似但受宠若惊的模式,SSv2-T更早地登顶(L15).
第二,没有文字的线性探测器(图3c)检查峰值位于视频嵌入本身. 外观控制保持从L25到输出的79 79,而相向动作则在L25达到高峰,而前向和逆向的RTime剪辑则在L15.
第三,我们在试验时间 封锁跨帧注意力: Lk意味着,从k层起,一个帧的令牌不能处理其他帧的令牌. 在Qwen上,以10.6 10.6和CiA-SSv2 Static 以8.7 8.7挡下L12下方的CiA-SSv2 Chilal,而以最多0.5.0.5挡下L24改变每分. 实习生VL的行为与L8和L20相同(附录F)。
因此帧被合并到L24之前,用于外观和时间,时间信息在中层或紧接中层后(Quen上的L15–L28)会达到顶峰,并会向输出方向淡出,而外观则不会. 这表明调整了结合帧的地层,而不仅仅是后期地层(H3).

blocks.en:
On Qwen, Ours keeps general R@1 and raises time-sensitive retrieval.
Against the base model, the unseen general R@1 (the five general benchmarks other than MSR-VTT) changes by − 0.02 -0.02 [ − 0.52 , 0.48 ] [-0.52,0.48] , and no single general benchmark changes significantly. Plain (LoRA) loses 3.8 3.8 [ 2.9 , 4.6 ] [2.9,4.6] on the same five, and Ours is above it on every general benchmark. RTime Hard rises by + 7.7 +7.7 [ 5.6 , 9.9 ] [5.6,9.9] and Binary by + 9.2 +9.2 [ 7.1 , 11.2 ] [7.1,11.2] .
The gains also hold on unseen benchmarks: CiA-Charades + 10.7 +10.7 [ 9.4 , 12.0 ] [9.4,12.0] and CiA-EPIC + 12.6 +12.6 [ 10.7 , 14.7 ] [10.7,14.7] . On Vinoground [ 53 ] , an unseen benchmark whose paired captions differ only in event order, Ours also raises the group score ( + 2.4 +2.4 [ 0.5 , 4.3 ] [0.5,4.3] ). Like the embedding models in [ 53 ] , all models stay below chance ( 16.7 16.7 ): a pair counts only if each clip prefers its own caption and each caption its own clip, so a model that prefers one caption for both clips always fails ( Appendix H ).
The CiA gains are on Chiral. Wider galleries give mixed results, and CiA-Charades Static falls by 5.1 5.1 [ 3.3 , 7.0 ] [3.3,7.0] (all galleries in Appendix G ).
Ours is slightly above Plain (LoRA) on CiA-Charades Chiral ( + 1.0 +1.0 ) and matches it on CiA-EPIC Chiral ( − 0.3 -0.3 ); Plain training stays ahead on SSv2-T, whose test queries are the training templates. So on unseen time-sensitive benchmarks Ours gains as much as Plain training but also keeps general retrieval.
On SSv2-Label, whose queries reword the training templates, Ours and Ours w/o pair loss rise by about 9 9 points on Qwen while Plain training stays near the base model: the keep loss lets what is learned from the templates transfer to new wording (on InternVL, all trained models rise alike).

About half of the CiA gain comes without the pair loss ( Tab. 1 ).
On top of Ours w/o pair loss, the pair-margin loss adds Hard + 4.6 +4.6 [ 3.0 , 6.2 ] [3.0,6.2] , Binary + 5.2 +5.2 [ 3.7 , 6.8 ] [3.7,6.8] , CiA-Charades + 5.1 +5.1 [ 4.4 , 6.0 ] [4.4,6.0] and CiA-EPIC + 6.0 +6.0 [ 4.9 , 7.2 ] [4.9,7.2] , without lowering general R@1, but not SSv2-T ( − 2.9 -2.9 [ − 8.6 , 2.7 ] [-8.6,2.7] ).
InternVL shows the same pattern: unseen general R@1 changes by + 0.7 +0.7 [ 0.1 , 1.2 ] [0.1,1.2] for Ours and by − 1.8 -1.8 [ − 2.7 , − 0.8 ] [-2.7,-0.8] for Plain (LoRA), and time-sensitive retrieval rises.

Our objective also works on all weights: RTime Hard 64.2 64.2 and general R@1 57.5 57.5 , against 50.1 50.1 for Plain (all weights). LoRA on the middle layers trains 0.15 % 0.15\% of the parameters (output heads trained in both) in less than half the training time of all-weight training ( Sec. A.1 ). Against all-weight training, it is lower on Hard ( − 1.0 -1.0 [ − 2.9 , 0.8 ] [-2.9,0.8] ), equal on unseen CiA and higher on general R@1 ( + 0.9 +0.9 [ 0.3 , 1.5 ] [0.3,1.5] ), so all-weight training goes further along the same trade-off. All weights are also higher on SSv2-T, whose test queries are the training templates.

blocks.en:
Tab. 2 compares Ours with the TARA recipe, released models and WiSE-FT under our protocol.
The TARA recipe, which fine-tunes on text alone, trades general R@1 for time-sensitive retrieval on the same Qwen model: at learning rate 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} it has general 44.8 44.8 and the best Binary among single models ( 75.1 75.1 ). With the TARA LoRA setting, general R@1 stays at 57.2 57.2 but RTime Hard barely rises ( 56.9 56.9 ), so no TARA setting is above Ours on both general R@1 and RTime Hard. TARA also reports a drop in general retrieval on its own protocol (MSR-VTT NegBench R@5 [ 1 ] : 79.8 → 70.2 79.8\rightarrow 70.2 [ 3 ] ).
With our keep loss on the text side, the TARA recipe recovers general R@1 to 57.8 57.8 , and Ours is higher on Hard ( + 3.4 +3.4 ), CiA-Charades ( + 9.9 +9.9 ), CiA-EPIC ( + 8.1 +8.1 ) and SSv2-T ( + 24.3 +24.3 ).
With a keep loss on both text and video, general reaches 59.2 59.2 , the highest in the table, but RTime Hard barely moves ( 57.9 57.9 ), so on general retrieval alone the TARA recipe can do better than Ours.
TARA reaches its best results on Tarsier2 (Tarsier2 alone: general R@1 12.3 12.3 in our protocol). The released Tarsier2 + TARA is ahead of Ours only on CiA-EPIC, at general R@1 48.4 48.4 , and the other released models are lower on every column ( Sec. I.2 ).
Ensembles with released TARA ( ⊕ \oplus ) raise RTime Hard further but need two models and a vector of twice the length. Ours is a better partner than the base model ( Sec. I.1 ).

blocks.en: WiSE-FT. Interpolating the weights of Plain training and the base model (WiSE-FT [ 48 ] ) also softens the trade-off. blocks.en: With one vector per clip, training for time-sensitive retrieval can keep general R@1. General R@1 tracks how close the output embeddings stay to those of the base model, not how far the weights move. This holds whether a keep loss keeps them close during training or weight interpolation restores them after training. Keeping the weights near their initial values during training (L2-SP or a lower learning rate) preserves less general R@1 than the keep loss. With a keep loss, a pair-margin loss that pushes each clip away from its reversed copy, and LoRA on the middle layers, a strong embedder gains about 8 8 to 13 13 points on RTime Hard and on opposite actions in unseen CiA, keeps most of its general retrieval even without general-domain data, and lies above WiSE-FT of Plain training. Middle-layer LoRA ( 0.15 % 0.15\% of the parameters) nearly matches training all weights on RTime and unseen CiA and keeps general retrieval better.

Each RTime and SSv2 query has two hard negatives: the reversed copy of its clip and one frame-shuffled copy of the forward clip (for the query of a reversed RTime clip: the forward clip and the shuffled copy). blocks.en:
CiA follows the official TARA protocol [ 3 ] : each class name is a query, every clip of the query class is a positive, and we report AP per class query, averaged over the queries. Chiral: the gallery holds the query class and its opposite class. Static: the gallery holds the query class and one non-opposite class from every other pair. All: the gallery holds every class. CiA is thus class-level retrieval, close to zero-shot classification. For example, Static ranks “putting a blanket somewhere” against “putting a broom somewhere”.
Our one change to the TARA code: our CiA-SSv2 queries fill the object noun of each template, while the raw TARA templates make several classes share one query string. Chiral is unaffected.
blocks.zh:
CIA遵循官方TARA协议[3]: 每个类名是一个查询,查询类的每个片段都是正数,我们报告每个类名的AP,平均于查询. Chiral:画廊持有查询类和相对类. 静态:美术馆持有查询类和从其他每对中分出一个非对等类. 所有: 画廊举办每门课. CiA因此是类级检索,接近于零发分级. 例如,Static将“在某地扔毯子”与“在某地扔扫帚”区分开来。
我们对 TARA 代码的一个更改: 我们的 CiA-SSv2 查询填充每个模板的对象名词,而原始 TARA 模板则使多个类共享一个查询字符串. 奇拉尔没有受到影响。

blocks.en: The 20 20 K training triplets of TARA are not released, so we rebuild them from license-free sources with the mix of the paper ( 20,000 20{,}000 text triplets: 8,000 8{,}000 core, 1,000 1{,}000 negation, 1,000 1{,}000 time, 10,000 10{,}000 multimodal). Core triplets come from the SimCSE NLI set, as in TARA; negation triplets are NLI triplets whose hard negative adds a negation, selected by a rule instead of an LLM; time triplets come from RTime training captions instead of Ego4D narrations; multimodal triplets come from WebVid-CoVR with the videos replaced by their captions. We copy the released trainer: contrastive loss with temperature 0.05 0.05 over groups of 256 256 triplets, optimizer batch 768 768 , AdamW with learning rate 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} , 10 % 10\% warm-up and linear decay, two epochs ( 52 52 steps), on all weights of the language model. The text format is that of our protocol, since the prompt TARA used on Qwen3-VL-Embedding is not released. Since its time triplets come from RTime training captions, the rebuild sees in-domain text for RTime, which favors the TARA recipe, not Ours, on RTime. To measure this effect, we also train the TARA recipe once with the 1,000 1{,}000 time triplets replaced by 1,000 1{,}000 further core triplets (one seed; an ablation, not a baseline). Against the full recipe with the same seed, it is higher on general R@1 ( 47.3 47.3 vs. 44.5 44.5 ) and RTime Origin ( 83.0 83.0 vs. 80.3 80.3 ) and lower on RTime Hard ( 53.8 53.8 vs. 56.5 56.5 ), Binary ( 66.3 66.3 vs. 74.7 74.7 ), CiA-Charades ( 61.8 61.8 vs. 68.1 68.1 ), CiA-EPIC ( 67.6 67.6 vs. 74.9 74.9 ) and SSv2-T ( 28.2 28.2 vs. 30.5 30.5 ). Each value lies outside the range of the full recipe over three seeds. blocks.en: This section gives a further control of the pair loss (paragraph “The pair loss” in Tab. 2 ): whether reversed queries generated for SSv2 and MSR-VTT clips give the pair loss a role for language.

blocks.en: We generate reversed queries with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct from the training caption alone (text only, greedy decoding). The prompt asks for a caption of the same clip played backwards: reverse the direction of every action, swap the order of events, keep the people, objects and setting, do not mention the reversal, and answer “NONE” when reversal would not change the description (a static scene, talking, a symmetric motion). The prompt gives seven hand-written examples, none from RTime. For SSv2 clips whose template has an opposite, the reversed query is the opposite template filled with the clip’s own objects, without the LLM. Outputs equal to the caption count as NONE. About 87 % 87\% of the SSv2 captions and half of the MSR-VTT captions get a reversed query. Examples: “uncovering pencil” → \to “covering pencil”; “a video of two women hugging” → \to “two women releasing their hug”. This section gives the full Vinoground results behind the sentence on unseen event order in Sec. 5 .
Vinoground [ 53 ] has 500 500 pairs of short clips and captions. The two captions of a pair use the same words with the events in the other order, and the two clips show the events in the two caption orders. We score Vinoground zero-shot with the retrieval embedding of each model ( Sec. 5 ). The text score counts a pair as correct when both clips prefer their own caption, the video score when both captions prefer their own clip, and the group score when both the text and the video conditions hold (chance 25 25 , 25 25 and 16.7 16.7 ). Table 13 gives the results. Ours is above the base model on all three scores (text + 4.9 +4.9 [ 2.1 , 7.9 ] [2.1,7.9] , video + 2.7 +2.7 [ 0.2 , 5.3 ] [0.2,5.3] , group + 2.4 +2.4 [ 0.5 , 4.3 ] [0.5,4.3] ), and above Ours w/o pair loss (text + 3.9 +3.9 [ 1.1 , 6.7 ] [1.1,6.7] , video + 1.9 +1.9 [ 0.2 , 3.7 ] [0.2,3.7] , group + 1.7 +1.7 [ 0.4 , 3.1 ] [0.4,3.1] ), so the gain of Ours over the base model comes mostly from the pair loss. All models stay below chance, as embedding models do in the original study [ 53 ] . blocks.en:
We evaluate each released model with its own model code, prompts and pooling, on our 16 16 frames, test subsets, query lists and metrics, so scores can differ from the original papers. Each embedding is L2-normalized. Tarsier2 + TARA and Tarsier2. The released TARA weights on Tarsier2-7B and zero-shot Tarsier2-7B use the TARA model class and prompts (“Summary above video in one word:” and “Summary above sentence in one word:”), with the last-layer state of the last prompt token; our 16 16 frames are passed through the TARA video path. Zero-shot Tarsier2-7B has general R@1 12.3 12.3 , RTime Hard 19.5 19.5 , Binary 53.7 53.7 , CiA-Charades 54.4 54.4 , CiA-EPIC 63.4 63.4 and SSv2-T 22.4 22.4 , so TARA training raises its general R@1 from 12.3 12.3 to 48.4 48.4 . In the zero-shot Tarsier2-7B run, 4 4 CiA-Charades and 5 5 CiA-EPIC clips could not be decoded (about 0.1 % 0.1\% and 0.2 % 0.2\% of each gallery); they stay in the gallery with a zero embedding. CaRe-7B. We use the encoder of the CaReBench code: the same one-word prompts, each frame duplicated so that one Qwen2-VL temporal patch covers one input frame, and the last-token state. The CaRe paper uses 32 32 frames. GVE-7B. The video side follows the GVE model card (last-token state; the GVE paper uses 8 8 frames). The card gives no query format, so we put the retrieval instruction of the GVE paper (Table 5 there) in the system turn and end each query with the end-of-text token; without this token the query embeddings collapse (MSR-VTT R@1 5.6 5.6 ). LamRA-Ret. We follow the official LamRA zero-shot code: “Summarize above video in one word:” for clips, and “Find an everyday video match with caption.” followed by the same summary prompt for queries (the official query prompt exists only for MSR-VTT and MSVD; we use it everywhere), with the state before the embedding token that LamRA adds. The official LamRA reader samples 2 2 frames per second; we feed our 16 16 frames.

blocks.en: WiSE-FT [ 48 ] interpolates the weights θ \theta after Plain training with the base weights θ 0 \theta_{0} : θ 0 + α ⁡ ( θ − θ 0 ) \theta_{0}+\alpha(\theta-\theta_{0}) . For LoRA we scale the LoRA update and the head update by α \alpha , which is exact; for all weights we interpolate every trained weight. Table 14 gives three seeds per point. WiSE-FT comparisons at equal or matched general R@1 interpolate the scores linearly between the two evaluated α \alpha that bracket it; the interpolation weight is set from the three-seed means and kept fixed in the bootstrap. With LoRA, the WiSE-FT curve of Plain training passes through Ours (diff loss) and stays below Ours. With all weights, the WiSE-FT curve of Plain training stays below Ours (all weights): at α = 0.5 \alpha=0.5 , its best point on RTime Hard, general R@1 is 0.8 0.8 [ 0.3 , 1.5 ] [0.3,1.5] lower, and so are Binary ( 2.2 2.2 [ 0.5 , 4.0 ] [0.5,4.0] ) and CiA-Charades ( 1.8 1.8 [ 0.8 , 2.9 ] [0.8,2.9] ); at equal general R@1 Ours (all weights) is higher on Binary ( + 3.0 +3.0 [ 1.4 , 4.6 ] [1.4,4.6] ), CiA-Charades ( + 2.9 +2.9 [ 1.9 , 3.9 ] [1.9,3.9] ) and SSv2-T ( + 7.8 +7.8 [ 1.4 , 14.1 ] [1.4,14.1] ), and not significantly different on Hard and CiA-EPIC. The WiSE-FT curve of Plain training also stays, at matched general R@1, below Ours (diff loss, all weights) on all columns but CiA-EPIC.
blocks.zh: WISE-FT [48] 将平原训练后的权重与基准权重相乘 : : 0 + α ⁡ (θ- θ0)\theta_{0}+\alpha (\theta-\theta_{0}). 对LORA来说,我们用α-α来缩放LORA的更新和头部更新,这是准确的;对于所有重量,我们插入每一个训练过的重量。 表14给出了每个点的三个种子. WISE-FT在等值或相匹配的普通 R@1 中将两个被评价的 α\α 之间的分数线性地插入它;插入权重由三种子方法设定并固定在靴子上. 与LORA一起,平原训练的WISE-FT曲线穿过了我们的(diff lose)并停留在我们的下方. 在所有重量下,平原训练的WISE-FT曲线都保持在Ours(所有重量):在α=0.5\alpha=0.5下,其在Rtime Hard上的最佳点为0.8 [0.3, 1.5] [0.3, 1.5] 更低,二等分数(2.2 2.2 [0.5, 4.0] [0.5, 4.0] )和 CiA-Charades (1.8 1.8 [0.8, 2.9] [0.8,2.9]);在等分数的R@1 Ours(所有重量)上,在Binary(+ 3.0 + 3.0 [1.4, 4.6] [1.4, 4.6])、 CiA-Charades (+ 2.9 + 2.9 [1.9, 3.9]) 和 SSv2-T (+ 7.8+7.8 [1.4, 14.1] [1.4,14.1] 在Hard和 CiA-EPIC上没有显著不同。 Plain训练的WISE-FT曲线也保留在除CiA-EPIC以外的所有列上,与一般R@1相匹配,低于Ours(diff损失,所有重量)。

blocks.en: We also train the pair-margin loss without the keep loss ( β = 0 \beta=0 ; general 54.7 54.7 ) and apply WiSE-FT to this model ( α = 0.25 \alpha=0.25 , 0.5 0.5 , 0.75 0.75 ; three seeds). At the general R@1 of Ours, this WiSE-FT curve reaches about the same point as Ours: Ours differs by + 0.4 +0.4 [ − 1.0 , 1.7 ] [-1.0,1.7] on RTime Hard, + 0.7 +0.7 [ − 0.5 , 1.9 ] [-0.5,1.9] on Binary, + 0.3 +0.3 [ − 0.3 , 0.8 ] [-0.3,0.8] and + 0.9 +0.9 [ 0.0 , 1.8 ] [0.0,1.8] on CiA-Charades and CiA-EPIC, and − 3.3 -3.3 [ − 9.3 , 2.8 ] [-9.3,2.8] on SSv2-T. Both hold the output embeddings near those of the base model (closeness 0.984 0.984 for Ours, 0.94 0.94 and 0.88 0.88 at α = 0.5 \alpha=0.5 and 0.75 0.75 ), and general R@1 follows closeness in both ( Sec. D.2 ). So the keep loss reaches, in one training run and without choosing α \alpha , the point that post-hoc interpolation of a no-keep model reaches, and the gain of Ours over WiSE-FT of Plain training comes from the pair loss.

D.2. ). 因此,在一次训练中,在不选择α-α的情况下,“保持”损失到达了“保持”模型的后插值,而“我们的WISE-FT”(Plain训练的WISE-FT)的收益来自“对接”损失。
